sections.text: Ausgaben (German for «expenses») is a mobile companion to the desktop finance software KMyMoney. Use it to record cash expenses, income and transfers on the go – right on your phone or a Wear OS watch – and transfer them into KMyMoney later, instead of typing everything in by hand.
The app works fully offline and without any vendor account: data is exchanged with KMyMoney through a folder you provide yourself (Nextcloud, WebDAV or SMB/Samba). There are no ads and no tracking.

items: Booking: a single money event (expense, income or transfer).
Account: e.g. «Cash», «Checking». Every booking belongs to an account.
Place (holding): where an account's cash physically is (wallet, jar, envelope …).
Category: what the money was spent on or received for (e.g. «Groceries»).
Alias: a learned mapping «spoken term → correct payee» together with account/category.
.kmy: KMyMoney's file format that is exported to and imported from.

content.text: As long as no account exists yet, a slim welcome assistant appears automatically when the app starts. It bundles the most important starting points in one place and can only be opened automatically (no menu entry).

items: Choose the language (takes effect immediately).
Import/export format: CSV or KMyMoney file (.kmy).
Synchronisation: server type, URL, user, password – with «Test connection»; in .kmy mode also «Choose .kmy».
«Import accounts»: the same selection dialog as «Add account», right here in the assistant.
«More settings» opens the full settings; «Done» closes the assistant.

sections.text: Important – an account first: create at least one account – in the assistant via «Import accounts» or later in the account drawer (☰ top left) via «Add account». The default account and the options that depend on it (e.g. places per account) can only be set once accounts already exist.

All settings in detail – language, number format, currency, server connection, export mode, default account, alias names, app lock, backup and more – are explained in the «Settings» chapter at the end of the manual (Chapter 16). They are reachable any time via the ⋮ menu at the top right, entry «Settings» at the very bottom.

content.text: The main screen shows the green title bar at the top, the balance line below it, and then the list of bookings. The action buttons are at the bottom right.

shot.caption: Main screen with title bar, balance line and booking list

content.text: The coloured line below the title bar shows a balance. Tapping it cycles through, in order:

items: Account: balance of the currently selected account (only when a single account is selected).
Total: sum of all accounts.
Net worth: all accounts + current portfolio value (only after a portfolio was imported).
Places: balances of the account's individual cash places.
Filtered: sum of the currently filtered bookings (only when a filter is active).

content.text: A green amount = positive/credit, a red amount = negative.

shot.caption: Balance line with group total; tapping cycles through

content.text: For the launcher there are four selectable widgets showing the default-place balance (default account → default place): small (2×1, balance only), medium (4×2, balance + three quick actions: booking, voice, amount), large (4×4, a balance header with refresh, the most recent bookings and the action bar) and type (4×2, like on the watch: three coloured income/transfer/expense icon buttons + a grey switch button, with the balance below). Tapping the balance opens the app; the medium/large widget buttons launch «New booking», voice entry, amount-only entry or Holdings. On the type widget a type button starts speech recognition immediately and creates the booking directly – the app is not opened (only the system voice dialog appears); the grey switch button cycles through the chosen account and its places (the balance and the target of the new booking follow the selection). The widget refreshes when the app is opened and at regular intervals.

shot.caption: All four widget sizes: medium, type, large and small

sections.text: This overview explains every symbol in the app and what it does.

items: Open it via the ☰ symbol at the top left, or by swiping in from the left edge.
«All accounts» shows all bookings together; a single account filters the list to it.
Long press on an account: import/update that account from the .kmy.
Long press on «All accounts» – or pull down in that view: reloads everything (accounts, portfolios and scheduled transactions) in one pass.
Portfolios sit at the bottom under the «Portfolios» heading and behave just like accounts: a short tap opens the portfolio view (the selected portfolio stays highlighted), a long press updates it.
«Add account» (at the bottom): loads the .kmy and offers the contained accounts for selection.

shot.caption: Account drawer with accounts, portfolio and «Add account»

sections.text: Besides the account kind (asset, liability, portfolio) there are account groups for your own ordering – «Favourites», «Joint» or «Savings», say. An account may sit in any number of groups; the grouping by account kind is unaffected.

items: Tap the «Accounts» heading and the groups drop down as a list. Each row carries the mark of its origin (a star for the favourites, a bank building for the groups from the .kmy, a folder for your own), and the one in force carries a tick. The drawer then lists only its accounts, and the top row carries the group name instead of «All accounts».
The chosen group applies app-wide: the booking list, the balance bar (as an additional first page there; «Total» still means all accounts) and the holdings view all follow it.
Removing the last account from a group (or deleting that account) makes the group disappear without asking – there are no empty groups. That is also how you get rid of a group again.
Groups holding nothing but closed accounts no longer show up in this picker. They stay selectable in an account's «⋮» menu so they can be revived.
The institutions block of the .kmy additionally yields bank groups (e.g. «Volksbank»). These merely mirror the file: only the import writes them, they cannot be edited by hand.

The «Favourites» group likewise comes from the file: it holds the accounts marked as preferred in KMyMoney (its account dialog, «Preferred account»). It sits at the very top of the picker, cannot be edited any more than the bank groups can, and is rebuilt on every import. Once no account is preferred any longer, it disappears. Its name follows the language of the app.

shots.caption: Afterwards the top row carries the group name

content.text: A magnifier sits on the kMyMoney emblem at the top of the drawer. Tapping it opens the keyboard, and for the duration of the search your input takes the place of the «Accounts» heading. What you type filters the account list instantly by part of the name – «kasse» thus also finds «Sparkasse» and «Barkasse».

Closing the keyboard puts the heading back in its place – but the term stays in effect, so the list still shows only the matches. The magnifier now carries a small cross to signal that a filter is on; tapping it lifts the search.
The search stays inside the chosen account group and is never stored. It also ends by itself as soon as you pick an account, close the drawer or leave the app.

shot.caption: The search field takes the place of the «Accounts» heading

content.text: The gear icon next to «Accounts» opens a view of its own. Unlike the drawer it also shows closed accounts, in grey, each with its balance on the right.

items: Drag the handle to sort accounts within their account kind. The order applies everywhere accounts are listed – including the pickers while recording a booking.
Drag a whole account kind: its accounts collapse for the duration of the drag and only their number is shown. That way even a large block reaches its place in a few movements.

«⋮» on an account row: your own account groups as a tick list. The tick says whether the account sits in that group; set and clear as many as you like, nothing is written until «OK». On top there is a free field for a new group – typing into it ticks its box by itself.

Groups from the .kmy (banks, favourites) are not in the list. Type one of their names into the free field and the dialog stays open with a note, writing nothing – an assignment by hand would be gone again at the next import anyway.
The same tick list carries, next to «OK», a «Close account» (or «Reopen account») button; it applies the ticks along the way. Close account is offered only at a balance of 0.
If a closed account regains a balance on import, it reopens by itself.

shots.caption: Management also shows closed accounts, greyed out, with balance
Dragging an account type folds its accounts away
«⋮»: tick groups, create a new one, close the account

content.text: Tap the round ✚ button. The booking editor opens.
Picking a value – the same everywhere

Payee, account, category and place fields are display, list and search box in one – in the booking editor just as in transfers, reconciliation, the filters, the alias editor, the settings and the analysis.

items: Entering the field: the current entry steps aside and stays on only faintly; the full list opens.
Typing: the list narrows as you go. Matches are found anywhere in the name and regardless of case – "kasse" finds "Sparkasse".
Deleting characters: the list widens again. Empty the field and everything is back.
Tapping an item: it goes into the field and the keyboard closes.

The Done key (bottom right on the keyboard): finishes the entry and closes the keyboard without you leaving the field. If typing leaves exactly one match, it is taken – "visa u" is enough for "Visa Urlaub". With several matches the same rule applies as when leaving the field.
Leaving without a choice: the previous entry returns.

content.text: A new payee may be created this way: type a name that does not exist yet and it stays. Account, category and place have to come from the list – an invented name is replaced by the previous one when you leave the field. New accounts arrive through the import, new places are created in the settings.

Account fields put what you are most likely to need at the top: first your favourites (star), then the accounts of the currently selected account group (the group's own icon), then all the rest with the icon of their account kind. Your own account order is kept within each block.

For the payee the location does the same: the six nearest payees head the list with a bearing arrow, the nearest one first. Distances are measured from the booking's location – whatever the location row shows: in a new booking your current one (only with location (GPS) switched on), while editing the booking's stored mark, and if you pick another point there via «Map», the block follows. A booking without a mark gets no block – where you stand today says nothing about an old booking. How far away a payee is comes from the same sources as the radius filter: the coordinates in the notes of its bookings and the learned locations of its aliases; the nearest point counts, and anything beyond 10 km does not appear. Below them the complete alphabetical list follows unchanged, so those six appear a second time. As soon as you start typing the block disappears and you see the alphabetical matches alone; delete what you typed and it is back. It does not appear when you view a planned booking.

Once the payee is set, the category follows from it: the app looks for entries of the currently selected booking type – first in the preferred aliases (★), then in your bookings for that payee (the most recent first, the parts of a split booking count too), finally in the remaining aliases – and puts the first find into the first category row; the partial amount jumps to the total. The preset follows the payee: if the app guessed him from the amount and you enter someone else, the category moves along – a second row from an alias gives way to the new payee's category as well. As soon as you have done something in the category rows yourself – picked or typed a category, changed a partial amount, removed a row – your entry stays put: from then on nothing is pulled in any more. When editing a saved booking (or booking a scheduled one) the category is left alone anyway, even if you change the payee there. The other categories found (up to six) head the list under the heading «FOR THIS PAYEE» – in every category row, so splitting benefits too. As soon as you start typing that block disappears and the categories only appear in their usual place under «EXPENSE» or «INCOME». Switching between expense and income switches block and preset with it; transfers have no categories.

The other way round, the amount can supply the payee: leave the amount field, and if within 100 m of the location mark there is exactly one payee whose usual amounts match it, that name goes into the empty payee field – bringing its category along. This applies to every booking type, transfers included – there compared against the amounts of your previous transfers to that payee. If several match, or none, nothing happens; a payee you entered yourself is never touched. The suggestion list itself is unaffected: it still lists every payee within 10 km. This pre-fill is off by default; switch it on under «Use amount for payee suggestions» in the settings.

shot.caption: Booking editor with type switch, amount, payee and account

sections.text: The amount field accepts a small calculation instead of the system keyboard (e.g. 10+20*3 or 30-5) – handy when splitting a bill or offsetting several items.

items: Type switch: Expense · Transfer · Income. Sets the kind of booking.
Amount, payee, account (chosen from existing accounts).
Date: pre-filled with today; the «Today» button quickly sets the current date.
Note: free text. With location enabled it automatically contains «GPS: lat, lon».
Place (only for expenses/income created in the app): which cash place the booking is credited to.
«Exported» toggle: marks whether the booking has already been exported.
Save as new: creates a new booking.
Update: saves changes to an existing booking.
Delete: removes the booking.

sections.text: Date prompt when copying: if you open an existing booking, leave the date unchanged and «save as new», the app asks whether the old date or today should apply.

In the «Split categories» section you can enter several categories with partial amounts. With one category the total and category amount are linked; with several, the sum must equal the total. Partial amounts may be negative.

content.text: Choose the type «Transfer», then the From and To accounts plus an optional payee. This creates a linked booking in both accounts (marked → or ← in the list). You can also choose a from-place and a to-place; then the respective place journal is updated (from-account −amount, to-account +amount). Both fields are preset with the default place of the respective account; «no place» leaves that side's journal untouched. Editing or deleting the transfer rolls the place movements back.

shot.caption: Detail view of a transfer with balance before/after

sections.text: KMyMoney has tags: freely maintained keywords such as «Holiday», «Business trip» or «Tax», any number of which a booking may carry. The app reads them when syncing with the KMyMoney file and writes them back on export – including when you change a booking that has already been transferred. Below the note field there is a «Tags» row for them: it names the tags, and once there are too many for one line, only their number.

The pencil symbol opens a small window listing every tag of this booking, each with its own delete cross; below it a field adds another one. It behaves like the category, account and payee fields – typing shows the matches, tapping one takes it. Only what already exists in KMyMoney can be entered: the app never invents a tag, an unknown name is discarded when you leave the field. The bin symbol on the row clears all tags of the booking in one go. None of this takes effect until you save the booking; leave the screen without saving and everything stays as it was.

Tags work the same for expenses, income and transfers; on a transfer both account sides carry the same ones, since in the KMyMoney file it is a single booking. On a scheduled booking the rule's tags can only be viewed, not changed – book it and they come along and can then be edited. If the app does not know any tags yet – before the first sync, say, or in CSV mode where there is no KMyMoney file – the whole row does not appear at all.

A long press on the ✚ button opens voice input. Say e.g. «barber 20 €»: the app looks for a matching template (payee, account, category, booking type) and opens it with today's date and the spoken amount. Payee search also finds similarly spelled names.

If there are several payees with the same name (e.g. «REWE location 1» and «REWE location 2») and the location is known, the app picks the geographically nearest one – both for existing bookings and for aliases with stored coordinates.

content.text: With location enabled, the keypad symbol appears at the bottom. Type just an amount: the app looks for a matching template at your current location – among the payees of the accounts on display – and shows the resolved payee before you even save.

Where several known payees share your location (petrol station and car wash, supermarket and bakery), the amount decides as well. Before you type, the field below states how many come into question; while you type, the name matching the amount appears: €8 is the car wash, €80 the petrol station. Tap the name to cycle through the remaining candidates and finally through «no payee» – then you fill it in later yourself. Whatever is shown when you confirm is what gets booked. Usual means the range holding nine out of ten of that payee's previous bookings. Nobody is ruled out: the amount only sets the order, you can always cycle through them all. If it fits none of the ranges, the one closest to it comes first – measured as a ratio, so that a payee with small amounts does not always lose against one with large ones: at €15 the range €20–100 beats the range €5–10, at €1 it is the other way round. Anyone with fewer than five bookings is not judged at all and falls in the middle. The same order decides when you only speak an amount – on the phone as from the watch; there the first one is taken without asking. And if only one payee is nearby, it appears even with an unusual amount – filling the tank once is no reason to leave the booking blank. Only payees of the accounts on display come into question: once you pick an account in the drawer (or an account group), anyone who so far has only been booked on another account stays out – even standing right next to them. An alias without an account of its own counts everywhere; on the watch the account picked there with the grey key applies. The amount only has a say here with the «Use amount for payee suggestions» switch on (off by default). Without it the nearest payee appears at once and stays put while you type – you then choose by tapping alone.

shot.fname: Buchung Betrag - Automatischer Empfänger anhand GPS.png
shot.caption: Amount-only entry: the payee is resolved via the current location

content.text: In the booking editor the «Receipt» button lets you take a photo of the receipt or pick one from the gallery (one photo per booking; can be turned off under Settings → Receipt photos). The image is stored privately on the phone and uploaded in the background to a «Belege» folder – with a sub-folder per year – inside your configured sync folder (WebDAV/Nextcloud or SMB); photos taken offline upload on the next app start with a connection. This works for every booking type, transfers included – the bank statement for a wire, say. As both sides of a transfer carry the same note, both accounts show the same receipt; you can attach and change it from either side.

The reference to the image is stored in the note as a «BELEG: …» tag, just like the GPS coordinates. Because the note survives export/import with KMyMoney, the app finds the photo again even after a re-import. In the editor the note field shows only your free text; GPS and the receipt appear as two separate read-only rows below it, each with an icon – the map icon opens the location, the receipt icon opens the photo (view) or the camera/gallery chooser (edit).

A booking can hold several pages – for the second half of a till roll or an invoice spanning multiple sheets. The camera icon in the receipt row appends another page every time; while editing, each page gets its own line with crop and delete. When merely viewing a booking one line is enough: the page count on the left, a single image icon on the right that opens the viewer.

Instead of a photo you may attach a PDF document – the invoice you downloaded, a bank statement, the confirmation of a transfer. The receipt dialog offers «Choose PDF document» for it and opens the device's file picker. Several documents per booking are possible; each gets its own line with a PDF icon. Tapping it opens the document in your device's usual PDF viewer, with all its pages; a PDF is never cropped, only attached or deleted. A booking carries either photos or documents – the other entry in the dialog stays dimmed until you have deleted the existing pages. A PDF is uploaded just like a photo, into the same year folder; the note records it as «BELEG (PDF): …».

shot.caption: While editing, each page gets its own row with crop and delete

content.text: The viewer is part of the app itself. Swiping pages through the receipt (the header counts along: «Page 2 of 3»), pinching and a double tap zoom in to read the small print; another double tap fits the image back in.

The images are uploaded into a «Belege» folder with one subfolder per year. It sits next to the KMyMoney file (in CSV mode inside the configured sync folder) – the same place the «Backup» folder appears in. The year folder follows the booking date; move a booking across new year and its images follow on the server. After switching phones the app fetches each receipt from there when you open the booking.
Delete a booking and its images disappear on the next app start – not right away, so that the «Undo» offered straight after deleting still brings the receipt back.

shot.caption: The built-in viewer counts along: «Page 2 of 3»

sections.text: Exporting the receipts of a filter

Inside the app receipt files are named after an identifier – enough for the app, useless for a human. Anyone handing a quarter's receipts to their accountant needs speaking names. That is what «Export receipts» in the menu (⋮) of the booking list is for. The entry only appears when a filter is set, because it refers to exactly that filtered selection: date range, payee, category, tag, amount – whatever you have chosen.

The app packs all receipts of those bookings into a ZIP file and then asks where to save it. Every file inside is named «date_payee_amount_bookingnumber_page», for example «2026-08-16_Bäckerei-Mayer_8_23_1487_p1.jpg». The date comes first so that the file manager sorts correctly by itself; the booking number makes sure that two purchases on the same day at the same shop for the same amount do not end up with the same name. Multi-page receipts keep their page count, PDF receipts their extension. For a transfer the shared receipt is packed only once, named after the outgoing side.

Receipts that are not on this device are fetched from the sync folder while packing – after switching phones that is the normal case. If that fails (no network, file not there), the app packs the rest anyway and tells you at the end how many were missing. If none of the filtered bookings has a receipt, you only get a short note and are not even asked for a location; if not a single receipt could be fetched, no empty file is created either.

content.text: Right after the shot the app asks whether you want to edit the image. «Keep as is» leaves the photo untouched – so you never have to bother. Later you can reopen the editor at any time via the crop icon in the receipt row.

In the editor you drag the four corners onto the bill. There are two modes: «Rectangle» cuts straight, leaving just a section of the image; «Trapezoid» lets you place each corner freely and then straightens a skewed photo into a clean rectangle. Two sliders adjust brightness and contrast – handy for faded till receipts. The preview follows every change immediately, and «Reset» restores the starting state.

The untouched original is not lost: on «Apply» the app keeps a separate file carrying «_original» in its name and uploads it as well. That backup stays for good – even after several rounds of editing the starting image is still there. Deleting the receipt removes the original too.

So when you edit an image a second time, the app asks: «Continue editing» works on the current version – handy to nudge the brightness without losing your crop. «Start from original» brings back the untouched photo when a crop turned out too tight. For an image never edited before, the question does not appear.

shot.caption: Editing: four corner points, «Rectangle»/«Trapezoid», brightness and contrast

content.text: If you change the recognized payee while saving, the app asks whether to remember the mapping as an alias – together with account, category and place (for transfers the from/to accounts and from/to places). So «mom 100 €» is later booked automatically to the real name with the right account/place. The category and place fields in the alias form behave like the booking editor (grouped category picker; a place field only for accounts that have places). Resolution order: preferred aliases (★) → bookings → remaining aliases.

An alias can hold any number of locations (e.g. several branches). In the alias form, «Add coordinate» adds a row with latitude/longitude and «Open map»; the minus button removes a coordinate. When resolving (amount-only/voice) the alias matches if the current location is near any of its coordinates. Re-learning an alias from a booking at another place appends the coordinate (it does not overwrite).

Below that sits «Usual amounts»: a two-handled slider defining which amounts are typical for this payee – the amount filter used when several payees share a location. The slider does not move in amounts but in ranks: the default 10–90 % drops a tenth of the previous bookings at each end, so a single outlier cannot stretch the range. The corresponding amounts are shown above and on the handle. Narrow it, and this payee only wins on very typical amounts; widen it to 0–100 %, and every amount it ever had counts. With fewer than five bookings the slider is greyed out – that few say nothing yet. The slider belongs to the booking type selected above: switch to income or transfer and it shows the amounts of that type. For transfers only the outgoing side counts – otherwise every amount would appear twice. The range always applies when only an amount was spoken; in the number pad and the booking editor it takes the «Use amount for payee suggestions» switch.

shot.caption: Managing alias names: spoken term → real payee

items: Short tap on a booking opens it as a read-only view (same layout as the editor, but without any editing): a large coloured heading shows the type (income = green, transfer = yellow, expense = red), and the balance before and after the booking is shown at the bottom. Long press opens it for editing.
In the list the note is truncated to at most two lines; in the editor the note field spans four lines.

Pull down (in an account or portfolio view): in the kmy variant the .kmy file is re-read and that account or portfolio is refreshed. In the CSV variant this is not available – there you refresh an account via the account menu (long-press the account in the drawer).
Markers: «Split», → / ← (transfer), «exported»; colours red/green.

Filter (funnel ▽): with a search field that searches payee, note and category (substring, case-insensitive – so you can find a booking by its note as well); plus category (as a tree), tag (only present when the app knows tags from the KMyMoney file; «All» clears the choice), amount (slider) and date from–to (slider in whole-month steps; type an exact day into the field). For the amount, expenses count negative and income positive; the slider runs from the largest expense on the left to the largest income on the right, with a thin mark showing the zero in between. It moves in shares, not in amounts: the right thumb at 90 % cuts off the largest tenth – so a single outlier no longer stretches the whole slider. For an exact bound, type it into the field. At the bottom – only with location (GPS) switched on – sits the Radius button: each tap steps through «off», 100 m, 500 m, 1 km, 10 km and back to «off». On a step only those bookings remain that were made within that radius of where you are now – the coordinates sit in the booking note, and where they are missing the learned location of the payee from the alias applies. Your position is captured once when you apply, so the list does not travel with you; if no position is known yet the list stays empty and the title line shows «Filter active (0)». «Reset» restores «Radius off», after which location no longer matters. With a filter set, the menu (⋮) also offers «Export receipts», which writes the receipts of exactly that selection into a ZIP file. The filter applies to the list and the analysis (the radius to the list only). With a category filter a split booking shows only the partial amount of the chosen category.
Undo: after deleting a booking, «Undo» appears briefly at the bottom – one tap recreates it. In the place journal the deletion and the recreation stay visible as movements. Transfers have no undo.
Long press on the app icon (home screen): «New booking» opens the editor directly.

shot.caption: Filter by search text, category, amount and period

items: Periods: day / week / month / year.
Views: single account, place or total.

With an account group selected in the drawer, it appears as its own view behind «Total» and «Total without portfolio»: only the accounts of that group, its portfolios included – the same figure as in the balance bar on the main page.
Zoom by gesture: horizontal = number of bars, vertical = Y axis.
Closed accounts count only in the total view (historical balance).

shot.caption: Analysis as a bar and line chart

content.text: The Categories page (menu ⋮ → Categories) shows the expenses per category – as a pie chart and below it as a list, sorted descending by amount. It complements the analysis (chapter 9), which only shows the development over time per account/place.

items: Month/Year toggle: current month resp. current year.

In both views you page through the periods by swiping – just like in the budget (right = back, left = forward); the header shows the displayed month resp. year centred and bold, with the previous and next one in grey to the left and right (tapping pages as well). Paging stops before the first booking period and after the current one.
The chart uses the full width and at most half the screen height; the list below scrolls on its own while the chart stays visible.
The slices are unlabelled; a tap shows category and amount in the centre, without a selection the total is shown there. The list additionally states the share in percent.
The analysis covers all accounts and lists only categories with expenses.
Split transactions count through their partial amounts (not twice), transfers are left out – the same data source as the budget page.

shot.caption: Category pie chart: «Where does my money go?»

sections.text: The calendar toggle at the top right adds the scheduled expenses due in the period (chapter 12) to the ones already made – including those that sit as a deduction inside a scheduled income, such as the capital gains tax on a dividend. Then:

items: The sum per category grows by the scheduled share; the list sorts by the new sum.
In the chart the already paid share appears in the category's strong colour, the scheduled share right next to it in the same, lighter shade – together they form one continuous sector.
Rows with a scheduled share can be expanded (arrow on the right), showing «Already paid» and «Scheduled» separately.
With the toggle on, the slider also pages into future months/years – which then show only scheduled values – up to the last scheduled occurrence.

sections.text: Each category has a fixed colour – regardless of its current position in the list. The palette icon at the top right opens the colour list: tapping a category opens the picker; «Default» restores the automatic colour. The assignment takes effect immediately in the chart and list.

content.text: The Budget page (menu ⋮ → Budget) puts the actual value against a per-category target. It answers the question: «Am I on plan?»
Where does the target come from?

items: Import from KMyMoney (a button in the settings): if your .kmy contains a budget, its values are taken as the target — month-accurate (monthly and month-by-month budgets are stored per month). Such targets are not editable.

Compute from history: sum of all previous years ÷ number of years with data. Automatic when the «compute budget internally» switch is on, otherwise via a button. These targets can be edited by a long press on a row.

content.text: Whether a category is income or expense follows from the .kmy file. A refund therefore reduces the expense category without turning it into income; a computed negative actual is clamped to 0.

shot.caption: Budget page: actual/target per category, with progress bars

items: Toggle year / month. The year view sums the months; the month view shows the displayed month's target against that same month's actuals. In month view you page through months with a swipe (or by tapping the grey previous/next month in the header).
Toggle main categories only / with subcategories (a main category sums its subcategories).
Income first, then expenses (large headers); main categories bold, subcategories indented. The right side shows «actual / target».

Under each category a slim bar: green when on plan, red when behind (width = share of the target used). Instead of a purely linear time comparison, the app learns each category's typical timing from the payment history: a one-time expense (e.g. a transit pass bought at the start of the month) is green as soon as it is within budget, while regular expenses (groceries) are still measured against the elapsed time. Without history the linear comparison applies (for income reversed).

content.text: The Scheduled transactions page (menu ⋮ → Scheduled transactions, shown only in .kmy mode) imports the standing orders / schedules set up in KMyMoney and shows them as one chronological list by due date. The schedules are not refreshed by the normal account import; they update only when you use the pull-to-refresh gesture on this page – with the familiar yellow progress banner.

items: Each recurring schedule is expanded into its individual occurrences (e.g. a weekly bakery appears several times) — from the stored next due date up to 2 years ahead.
Only active schedules; entries without a date are skipped, and an end date (or a limited number of payments in KMyMoney) limits the preview.

A coloured strip precedes each row: green = deposit, red = payment, yellow = transfer. The date is its own column at the front, next to it the name with the payee in smaller, grey text behind it and below it the category (with several categories «Split transaction»), then an account column and the amount on the right. For a transfer the account column shows both accounts, one below the other (instead of a category).
The type comes from KMyMoney: a stock/ETF purchase (savings plan) is a transfer from the cash account into the security, not an expense.
A tap on a row opens the transaction in the familiar detail view (read-only, exactly like a real account movement – including the categories of a split transaction and the balance before/after).

Book now: a long press on a row opens the booking editor as a new booking, prefilled from the schedule (date = due date, amount, payee, account, categories resp. from/to). Check it, adjust if needed and save with «New booking» – it lands in the account and (with a place chosen) in the holdings. Tap = view, long press = book – just like in the booking list.
Skip booking: the prefilled editor also offers a «Skip booking» button (with a confirmation) – no transaction is created, but the date still counts as done.

The schedule moves on. Booked or skipped, the date disappears from the list right away, and on the next .kmy export the KMyMoney schedule is moved on by one period (for an actual booking the date of the last payment is written as well). The schedule itself – amount, rhythm, splits, start date – stays unchanged, and so do later dates. Cancelling the editor leaves the schedule as it is.

shot.caption: Scheduled transactions: chronological list with balance strip

sections.text: If you want, the app reports once a day when something is due today («3 scheduled transactions due today»); tapping the notification opens this page. The switch «Remind me of due transactions» is in the settings and is off by default; when switching it on the app asks once for the notification permission. If nothing is due, no notification appears.
At the top – like in the normal account view – a balance strip (label on the left, amount on the right) that always reflects the currently set filter. Each tap cycles the display:

items: Surplus or deficit (default) = total deposits − total bills; only the applicable state is shown (green = surplus, red = deficit).
Total deposits (green).
Total bills (red).
Transfers (yellow) = sum of all scheduled transfers.

sections.text: Transfers count towards neither deposits nor bills (they only move money between your own accounts) and therefore have their own line.
The filter icon at the top right narrows the list (and thus also the balance strip and the chart) by:

items: Type: deposits, bills, transfers (each can be toggled on/off).
Account: single selection from a list of all accounts (or «All accounts»).
Name: search text matched against name or payee.
Period: slider (month granularity) or direct, day-precise date entry.

content.text: The chart icon at the top right opens an analysis that looks exactly like the account view's chart: green/red bars for deposits and bills and a development line of the selected account or of total wealth. You can pick the view (total or a single account) and the time unit day/week/month. The line starts at the far left at today with 0 and runs to the right into the future; like the account chart it can be zoomed and panned. The chart inherits the list filter. For a transfer the amount decreases on the source account (red) and increases on the target account (green) – the direction («pay to» or «from») is taken from KMyMoney.
When you scroll far down, the scroll-to-top button (bottom left) jumps straight back to the start of the list.

shot.caption: Chart of the plans: bars per due date and a development line

content.text: A place describes where an account's cash physically is – e.g. wallet, jar, petty cash or an envelope. An account «Cash» can thus be split into several real storage locations. This feature does not exist in KMyMoney; it is an addition of this app for everyday cash handling.
Places are not limited to cash accounts – they can be used for any account. In the following examples we stay with cash, though.

Reached via ⋮ → Holdings. Each place keeps its own movement journal; its balance is the sum of its movements. The sum of all place balances always equals the account balance: «no place» is the automatically computed remainder (account balance − sum of the other places). So the account stays consistent no matter how many places you create.

shot.caption: Holdings: asset/liability accounts and portfolio, with places per account

items: A booking created in the app automatically produces a movement on the account's default place.
Place movements can be created, edited and deleted individually.
Money can be transferred between places (e.g. to assign an imported booking to a place, or to move cash from the envelope into the wallet).
Later amount or deletion changes append dated balancing movements – the history is preserved.

sections.text: A transaction that was exported and imported again loses its place link – that is intended. If you still open such a transaction for editing (long press), the place field is shown as soon as the account has any places, so you can pick one. What happens then depends on the button you press:

items: «New transaction» (duplicate): a new transaction is created – the chosen place is saved and a movement is added in the holdings. This is the way to give an old transaction a place afterwards.
«Update transaction» on a transaction that had no place before and is already exported: the entered place is ignored, the place journal stays untouched.
«Update transaction» on a transaction that had a place before: the new place is saved and followed up with balancing movements (old place −amount, new place +amount).

sections.text: In the plain view (short tap) the place field only shows up if the transaction really sits at a place – a «no place» would tell you nothing, and an imported transaction has none at all. For transfers that holds for the from-place and the to-place each on its own; the movement is created on both accounts.

A particular advantage: the cash count (reconciliation) can be done per place. You count only the cash of one place – say the wallet – enter the counted amount, and the app automatically books the difference as a balancing movement. So you don't have to reconcile the whole account at once; this simplifies reconciliation considerably. Imported bookings carry no place link. If an account has no places at all, the place field is missing and the whole account is reconciled.

Next to the «Create booking» switch there is a button for the payee and category of that balancing booking. Both are empty at first and the button reads «Set payee/category»; as long as nothing is set, «Apply» stays greyed out. The button opens a small dialog with both fields (with the same suggestion lists as in the editor); «Save» keeps them permanently, so the next cash count already has them prefilled.

Accounts are grouped by their KMyMoney type into asset accounts, liability accounts (loans, credit cards) and portfolios – with colour-coded section headers (assets green, liabilities red, portfolios blue; light theme → lighter colour/black text, dark theme → darker colour/white text) both in the account drawer and in the holdings view. In holdings each category header shows its category total right-aligned; the portfolio counts as one line (portfolio value) towards the total (in a neutral grey/black). The split comes from the .kmy.

content.text: After importing a KMyMoney investment account, the portfolio appears in the account drawer. The portfolio view is laid out like an account view – same title bar with the same menu items, same drawer, same filter – and shows shares × price = current value per security; fully sold securities are hidden. The balance line toggles by tap through portfolio value → buys → sells (if any) → dividends (if any) → net invested (buys − sells − dividends) → gain/loss (coloured, with percentage). The portfolio filter narrows the securities by name and value; like in the booking filter the slider works in shares, not in amounts. When you scroll far down, the scroll-to-top button (bottom left) jumps straight back to the start. A tap on a security opens its movements full-screen (buys green, sells red, dividends neutral) with the same figures for that security plus a filter by buys/sells/dividends and a date slider (start date = first purchase). The portfolio value is kept separate and also appears as «Net worth» in the main screen's balance line.

For Add and Remove transactions, KMyMoney only ever records a share count, never a monetary value. A long press on such a row opens a dialog to set the value manually (using the same calculator keypad as elsewhere) – it then counts like a buy or sell towards the cost basis and gain/loss, and survives a fresh portfolio import.

shot.caption: Portfolio view: securities with shares, price and current value

shots.caption: Movements of a security: buys, sells and dividends

content.text: The «Analysis» menu opens a pie chart of the securities – styled like the Categories page (continuous ring, a fixed colour per security, at most half the screen height, with its own scrollable list below). The slices are unlabelled; a tap shows the name and amount of the security in the centre, with nothing selected it reads «Total». Chart and list are always sorted descending by the current value of the period.

At the top an icon toggle picks the view: Current value (default, € symbol) · Net deposits (arrow) · Total dividends (% symbol) · Gain/loss (trend arrow). Below it a period filter narrows the analysis – a monthly range slider (first portfolio transaction to today) plus two From/To date fields for any date. Any change to the view or period updates chart and list immediately.

shot.caption: Portfolio analysis: icon toggle, period filter and pie chart

items: Current value: today's value (current price) of the positions built in the period – i.e. the shares bought within the period that are still held. Over the full period this equals the current portfolio value (shares sold again within the period do not count negative).
Net deposits: buys − sells − dividends within the period.
Total dividends: all dividends received within the period (gross/net per the setting).
Gain/loss: current value − net deposits, per security as a € amount and as a % return on cost basis (buys) – coloured green/red in the list. The pie-chart slices keep the security's normal colour.

sections.text: In the toolbar an icon shows or hides fully sold securities (hidden by default). What counts is the net holding at the end of the selected period – a sale after that does not yet count as «fully sold».

Dividends gross/net: the settings let you choose whether dividends are shown gross (declared dividend) or net (cash received after tax) and used in the balance line (dividends, net invested, gain/loss).

content.text: The actual sync with KMyMoney runs through a single symbol in the main screen's title bar – the export/sync symbol (down arrow).

pic.caption: The export/sync symbol in the title bar (circled in red)

sections.text: Tap the export symbol ⬇. The app loads the current .kmy from the sync target, inserts your new bookings, makes a backup first (see below) and writes the file back. Each booking is exported only once and then marked «exported». In CSV mode one CSV file per account is uploaded instead.

Edited bookings. Change a booking that is already marked «exported» and it carries «edited» afterwards (yellow in the list). The next export does not add a second transaction: the existing one in the .kmy file is changed instead – the same transaction in the same place, no duplicate; the booking then reads «exported» again. You cannot set this status yourself: it only arises from a change, and the «Marked as exported» switch in the booking editor is locked and relabelled accordingly. If you switch it off yourself while editing, your choice wins: the booking is «not exported» and will be written as a new transaction on the next export. If the old transaction is no longer in the file (deleted on the computer, say), the message says so and the booking stays «edited» – nothing is inserted. Re-import the .kmy file in between and the file wins: the edit is gone. Transfers behave the same way even though they consist of two rows: in the file they are one transaction and are changed once.
Import is done selectively via the account drawer (long press):

items: Long press on an account: imports/updates exactly that account from the .kmy.
Long press on «All accounts» (or pull down in the «All accounts» view): reloads everything – accounts, portfolios and scheduled transactions, from a single download.

«Add account»: fetches an account not yet present from the .kmy. In the picker you can tick several accounts (and portfolios) at once; already-imported accounts (including closed) and portfolios are hidden.
Long press on the portfolio (or pull-to-refresh in the portfolio view): updates securities and prices – also in the background with the yellow progress banner.

sections.text: Securities buys and sells (money from the account into a security or back) are imported as a transfer into/out of the security. The small fee (or tax) inside the transaction does not appear in the booking list and changes no balances – but it is counted as a small expense in the category evaluations (chapter «Where does my money go?» and Budget). Dividends stay normal income.

An import replaces the already-exported bookings per account (no duplicates). The import runs in the background – the UI stays usable; a yellow banner at the top of the booking list («Importing account …») with a moving gradient, status text and percentage shows the progress and disappears when done. A message appears only on error. In CSV mode with SMB/WebDAV, adding an account or long-pressing one opens a navigable folder browser (subfolders 📁 + CSV files, «..» to go up); the chosen CSV is imported from the current folder. The drawer stays open on long press.

Before every write-back the app automatically creates a timestamped backup of the .kmy (e.g. file.kmy.bak-YYYYMMDD-HHMMSS). The backups go into the «Backup» subfolder next to the original; the folder is created automatically the first time. So you always have a fallback in case something is ever wrong with the file, and the actual folder stays tidy.

A few seconds pass between downloading the .kmy and writing it back. If somebody works in KMyMoney on the computer during that window, their changes must not be lost. The app therefore remembers the state of the file when downloading and only writes if it is unchanged.

If the file changed in the meantime, the export aborts and writes nothing; the bookings stay unexported and can be exported again after a fresh import, without any loss. If the server reports no state, the app writes unchecked – the export never fails because of this.

content.text: With the watch app you record an expense by voice right on your wrist. The watch only captures the text; processing and creating the booking happen on the phone.

items: Three type buttons: income (green), transfer (yellow), expense (red). Then voice starts.
The recognized text is shown briefly with «Cancel» and otherwise processed automatically.
Silent digit entry: enter an amount silently via the digits symbol (resolved by location on the phone).
Wear tile: quick access as a tile.

Default-place balance: below the buttons, the app and tile show the balance of the default place as «Place: balance» (e.g. «Wallet: 70.00 €»). The balance updates automatically. No default place set → line hidden.

Reason instead of balance: while bookings are not yet transferred, this line shows the reason instead of the balance – «Waiting for GPS» (the location is still being resolved), «No connection to phone» or «Transferring…». The line below still states the count.

Switch account/place: above «Record booking» (centred), a grey switch button – in the app and the tile – cycles through the shown account and its places; the next booking (phone widget and watch) then targets the chosen account/place. For a transfer the chosen account is the from-account; the to-account is the default account – unless the chosen account already is the default, in which case the to-account stays empty (to fill in manually on the phone). After a short while the selection reverts to the default place.
Offline: bookings not yet transmitted are shown and delivered automatically once the phone is reachable – without loss and without duplication.

shot.caption: Recording on the watch

sections.text: Speech recognition uses the language chosen in the settings (including uploaded ones) and prefers offline recognition, so recording works even without the phone/network – provided an offline speech model is present on the watch. If offline speech fails, the watch automatically opens the number pad: you just type the amount, the booking is buffered including GPS and sent automatically once the phone is reachable again (the payee is resolved by location on the phone).

So that voice recording works offline, the offline speech model of the chosen language can be installed on the watch. On the phone, enable the setting «Install offline speech package on the watch» (only in the GitHub build with the Wear bridge). On Wear OS 4+ the watch then triggers the download automatically (once, when a network is reachable); on older watches a hint appears to load the model in the watch's system settings. Without this switch, the number-pad fallback applies.
Requirement: the phone and watch apps share the same signature (same key).

content.text: The settings are reached via the ⋮ menu at the top right – entry «Settings» at the very bottom. On first start the welcome assistant (Chapter 2) already sets the essentials; here all fields are described in screen order. Changes take effect on «Save» (language and dark mode immediately).

shots.caption: Export mode, default account, places per account

items: Language: German/English (more via a language file). Pre-selected from the phone on first start; the choice takes effect immediately. Via «Export/upload language template» you can maintain your own translation as a file.
Currency: default currency symbol for accounts without their own currency (taken per account from the file on .kmy import).

Number format: «1.234,56», «1,234.56» or «1234,56»/«1234.56» without grouping; plus the «Show currency symbol» toggle. Applies to all amounts in the app and on the watch; the export keeps a stable format.
Dividends gross/net: whether portfolio dividends are settled gross (declared) or net.
Budget in-app: compute the budget actuals from history instead of importing from KMyMoney (see Chapter 11).

Install offline speech package on the watch (GitHub build with the Wear bridge only): lets the watch download the offline speech model of the chosen language so voice recording works offline too (see Chapter 15). Off → the number-pad fallback applies offline.

sections.text: Connection to your server (SMB / WebDAV / Nextcloud)
The most important setup step, so the app can exchange data with KMyMoney. Choose the server type and enter the access:

items: Nextcloud: base URL of the server + app password (Nextcloud → Security → App password).
WebDAV (generic): full DAV root URL, auth via HTTP basic.
SMB/Samba: set up through a wizard – see below. SMB2/3.
«Test connection» checks the credentials.

content.text: With server type SMB/Samba a wizard replaces the address fields, so you don't have to remember host or share names:

items: 1. Search for servers: on opening, the app scans the local network automatically (Bonjour/mDNS, a NetBIOS name query and a connection test on the SMB port). Each hit is listed with its display name and the IP address below it – plus its workgroup if the server reports one. «Search again» restarts the scan; the servers found last time are remembered and shown right away.

2. Log in: username and password of the server, with a «Port» field above them – leave it empty as long as the server listens on the usual SMB port 445. If it announces a different port over Bonjour, that port is already filled in; if nothing answers there, the app also tries the default port 445 and corrects the stored address. An empty user means guest. For a share without a password simply leave the password field empty – the app then continues as guest, even with a user name filled in. If the server belongs to a workgroup other than «WORKGROUP», the field is pre-filled with «WORKGROUP\». The password is stored encrypted and never shown in clear text.

3. Pick the share: after logging in the app reads the server's shares and offers them for selection (system shares such as IPC$ are hidden). Clicking one fills the «Share name» field; you can also type it there if the server refuses to list them.

4. Save: this becomes the address «smb://host/share» – with a different port «smb://host:7777/share». The target folder inside the share is then chosen as usual with the «Browse folder» resp. «Choose .kmy» buttons.
«Enter server manually» brings back the classic fields (type «smb://host/share» resp. «smb://host:port/share» yourself). «Search for servers on the network» returns to the wizard at any time.

content.text: Workgroup or Windows domain: at home the workgroup is usually called «WORKGROUP» – it plays no role for signing in, Samba servers and NAS boxes only check user and password. It is different in a real Windows domain (Active Directory): there you enter the user as DOMAIN\user (or as «user@domain.local»). Without the domain the login may fail with «Username or password is invalid» even though the password is correct. For a Windows PC with a local account, «COMPUTERNAME\user» helps.

If something fails, the wizard names the reason: «Server not reachable», «Username or password is invalid», «The selected share is not available» or «Access to the folder was denied» – followed, in brackets, by the server's raw status code, so a report can actually be traced. «Server not reachable» only ever appears while no connection has been established yet. If the port field does not hold a number between 1 and 65535, it says so right away without trying to connect.

shot.caption: SMB wizard: servers found, sign-in and share selection

content.text: The button «Check connection (diagnostics)» – in the settings and in the first-start wizard – walks the whole chain in one login and shows, for every step, whether it worked, how long it took and, on failure, the raw status code:

items: Connect (noting it if the default port was used instead of the configured one),
Negotiate: which SMB dialect, whether the server requires signing and whether encryption was negotiated,
Log in: as a user or as guest, encrypted or not,
Read shares, open share, read folder,

Write in the folder – the app creates a tiny test file and deletes it right away. A read-only directory would otherwise only surface when writing back, that is after you have already recorded bookings.
Check the file and, if it exists, whether it is writable (.kmy mode only).

content.text: «Copy report» puts the result on the clipboard – meant for sending along with a bug report. The report contains neither the password nor the user name (only «set» or «empty»).

shot.caption: Diagnostics: every step with duration and status code

items: .kmy mode: writes new bookings straight into the KMyMoney file (including splits and transfers) and imports accounts/bookings as well as the portfolio from it. «Choose .kmy» opens a file browser (subfolders, «..» to go back).
CSV mode: exports one CSV file per account (each booking only once); the target folder and import folder are set here.

sections.text: Without a configured sync target, export goes locally into a folder you choose. How the sync runs is in Chapter 14.

items: Default account: pre-selection for new bookings (also for widget and watch). Selectable only once accounts exist.
Places per account: per account you can create cash places and set a default place (see Chapter 13).

sections.text: The «Prompt» toggle controls whether the app offers to learn an unknown payee as an alias after you speak (existing aliases still apply). Via «Manage alias names» you create, edit and delete aliases by hand – with spoken term, real payee, booking type, account, categories and location (via «Open map» on an OpenStreetMap map). The «prefer» toggle (★) puts an alias ahead of the booking search; the same term may point to several payees distinguished by location.

items: Dark mode: light/dark (takes effect immediately).
Reminder for scheduled bookings: reminds once a day of scheduled bookings due today (off by default; see Chapter 12).

App lock: optional via biometrics/device credential (fingerprint, face, PIN, pattern, password) – on start and when returning from the background. When the app hands over to another app itself – camera, gallery, file picker, speech input – returning within five minutes does not ask again. Stay away longer and the lock is back.

Location (GPS) switch (default off): controls all location use. Off = no permission prompt, no GPS note, no amount-only entry, no alias location. The position is used locally only, never sent to a service.

Use amount for payee suggestions (default off): on = the amount helps decide where several payees share a location – in the number pad the name shown changes with the amount, and the booking editor pre-fills an unambiguous payee. Off = both stay quiet; the number pad shows the nearest payee, which you change by tapping. Regardless of this switch, plain voice entry without a payee – on the phone as from the watch – always uses the amount, because there is nothing to choose there.
Export all and Create/restore backup (see below).

Manage accounts (delete/close): a multi-select lists all accounts with status (Active/Closed). The bottom row has (context-dependent) Close/Reopen and, on the right, Delete; Close only at balance 0, Reopen only for closed accounts. A closed account no longer appears anywhere – only in the total analysis view does its historical balance still count.
Reset data: deletes the local database (a fresh start like the first time – the welcome assistant appears again afterwards).

sections.text: «Create backup» writes data and settings into a ZIP file: the database (bookings, accounts, place journal, portfolio, schedules) and all settings – including the places per account, the category colours and the server access. Beforehand the app asks two things:

items: Include the server password? No by default – then the password appears nowhere in the file and is entered once after restoring.
Backup password (optional, entered twice): it encrypts the whole file (AES-256-GCM, file extension .abk instead of .zip). Without a password it stays a plain ZIP.

sections.text: On «Restore backup» the app first asks for the backup password if needed, and then what should come back: data only, settings only or both. That way a broken configuration can be repaired without touching the recorded bookings. The app restarts afterwards. Receipt photos are not part of the backup – once uploaded they live on the server.

This app is provided as-is, with no warranty. In particular, there is no guarantee that the .kmy file remains fully valid after an export. Thanks to the automatic backup before every export, however, you always have a fallback. Keep your own regular backups as well.
German locale: column separator «;», decimal separator «,», date DD.MM.YYYY, UTF-8. Split bookings are written as one line per category.
